subject: MAP draft — Conformance checkpoints and fail-fast thresholds
messages:
From: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
To: alex@paywell.com, tara@paywell.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-23T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: MAP draft — Conformance checkpoints and fail-fast thresholds

Alex / Tara,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As promised, I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan that centers the evaluation on concrete acceptance tests rather than open-ended "evaluation" objectives. Primary goals here are: (1) define the high-confidence exit gates we need to move from POC to pilot, (2) list specific acceptance tests and owners, and (3) a short "fail-fast" rubric so we can de-risk early and avoid sunk effort if major blockers surface.

High-level asks for PayWell:
- Review the acceptance tests (sheet 2) for technical and product alignment.
- Confirm the latency/throughput targets you want enforced in the acceptance criteria.
- Call out any compliance traces you need for the SOC2/Pseudonymization checks.

Proposed timeline (draft):
- Week 0 (Aug 24–28): finalize MAP and test cases, legal/procurement kickoff
- Week 1 (Aug 31–Sep 4): smoke tests / integration connectivity
- Week 2 (Sep 7–11): canary evaluation run (10k queries), acceptance runbook
- Week 3 (Sep 14–18): decision and next-step signoff

Attached: paywell-map-v1.xlsx (MAP + ownership) and an initial evaluation-test-cases.md. I want to keep the MAP intentionally short — the spreadsheet is the single source of truth for owners and pass/fail criteria.

Next step: can we lock in a 30-min alignment on Mon Aug 24 10:00am PT to finalize the acceptance thresholds? If that works, I’ll send an invite and add the canary run dates to the calendar.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: paywell-map-v1.xlsx, evaluation-test-cases.md
From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com, karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-08-23T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: MAP draft — Conformance checkpoints and fail-fast thresholds

Laura / team,

Quick internal notes after skimming the MAP. I added a short technical appendix in the evaluation-test-cases.md that maps each acceptance test to measurable signals. A few concrete suggestions:

1) Exit gate: "Integration complete" should require an authenticated end-to-end request from PayWell staging to Redwood with KV-caching enabled and sample payloads. Owner: PayWell eng (Alex).
2) Latency SLA for acceptance: 95th percentile < 350ms for typical payloads (unless PayWell prefers tighter). If we want < 200ms we need extra batching/replica capacity and that should go into the cost/ops bucket.
3) Quality acceptance: 85% intent-match for NLU classification tests on the labeled set (I added a sample conformance script).
4) Fail-fast triggers: more than 2 critical test regressions in a 48h window => pause canary and triage.

I also flagged required artifacts for SOC evidence: request logs for a 7-day window, API audit traces, and the retention policy doc. Karthik, can you review the SOC checklist and confirm the KMS/HSM notes?

Ben
Ben Carter
Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference

Laura / Ben / Karthik,

Thanks for the draft. Overall this looks good and the structured acceptance tests are exactly what we need. A few clarifications from PayWell engineering:

- Latency: narrow to 95th percentile < 300ms on the staging workload (we'll send a sample corpus this afternoon). 300ms gives us breathing room for UX expectations.
- Throughput: canary should sustain 50 qps for a 10k request window without degradation.
- Quality: for the intent classification we want a two-tier check: overall intent-match >= 85% AND critical-intent recall >= 92% for the four critical flows we outlined on the call.
- Data handling: please confirm that session tokens and audit logs will be retained for 30 days in our staging environment; production retention will be addressed in procurement.

We can take the Aug 24 10:00am PT slot to finalize thresholds. Also looping in procure@paywell.com for early procurement signal on reserved capacity and contract cadence.

Alex Romero
Head of Engineering, PayWell
alex@paywell.com

Alex / Tara,

Great — thanks for the specificity. I updated the evaluation-test-cases.md (attached) and tightened the latency target to p95 < 300ms and added the canary throughput target (50 qps, 10k window). Summary of updates and owners: 

- Integration verification (owner: Alex, PayWell Eng) — test script in sheet 3 of the MAP
- Latency acceptance (owner: Ben Carter, Redwood) — p95 < 300ms on the provided corpus
- Quality acceptance (owner: Marissa Cole, Redwood + PayWell product) — two-tier check; dataset in Drive link
- Compliance artifacts (owner: Karthik Iyer) — 7-day staging logs + 30-day session retention confirmation

Schedule I just posted to the shared calendar (canary run: Sep 7–9; cutover decision meeting: Sep 16 10am PT). Please review and accept the calendar invite. If procurement needs lead time, procure@paywell.com is on copy.

Fail-fast rubric (short):
- Immediate stop and triage if: any critical-intent recall < 88% OR stability regressions causing >10% error rate sustained for 1 hour.
- Pause canary and roll back to baseline if 2+ critical failures in 48 hours.

Next actions:
1) PayWell: share sample corpus + staging credentials by EOD Aug 26.
2) Redwood: run smoke connectivity tests Aug 31–Sep 1 and share log template.
3) Procurement: confirm preferred billing cadence and reserved capacity window.

Thanks — will sync on Mon.

Laura Bennett
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
